edges.description: The knockout reproduces the genetic lesion, loss of Emc10, and shows mild behavioural and motor changes, but not the cognitive phenotypes tested.
edges.limitations: Homozygous Mirta22/Emc10 knockout mice showed no change in prepulse inhibition, working memory or social memory, and neither line has been assessed for intellectual disability-like or seizure phenotypes. In mouse, Emc10 is characterized mainly as an inhibitor of neuronal maturation whose excess, not loss, produces deficits, which does not match the human recessive loss-of-function disorder.

nodes.description: The EMC inserts transmembrane domains of tail-anchored and multipass membrane proteins into the ER membrane. EMC10 sits on the lumenal side of the complex. Whether EMC10 deficiency lowers or raises insertion of EMC clients in neurons is unknown: the disease-gene reports propose reduced insertion, while knockdown in human cell lines increased insertion of tail-anchored clients. The node is stated as altered insertion for that reason, and the process term carries no direction.

biological_processes: tail-anchored membrane protein insertion into ER membrane

evidence.reference_title: The ER membrane protein complex is a transmembrane domain insertase.
evidence.snippet: Purified EMC in synthetic liposomes catalyzed the insertion of its substrates in a reconstituted system.

evidence.reference_title: An engineered transcriptional reporter of protein localization identifies regulators of mitochondrial and ER membrane protein trafficking in high-throughput CRISPRi screens.
evidence.snippet: While loss of other EMC subunits decreased the ER localization of our mutant TA protease, EMC10 knockdown produced the opposite effect, which we confirmed by immunofluorescence and FACS.

nodes.description: Biallelic truncating or splice-site EMC10 variants reduce EMC10 transcript levels in patient blood, and the recurrent frameshift encodes a truncated protein that is degraded by the proteasome in transfected cells. The truncation removes the C-terminal region through which EMC10 contacts the core EMC. The molecular function lost is assumed to be EMC10's contribution to EMC membrane insertase activity; this assumption is contested (see the REFUTE evidence and the knowledge-gap discussion).

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic loss of EMC10 leads to mild to severe intellectual disability.
evidence.snippet: Utilizing exome sequencing and international data sharing we have identified 10 affected individuals from six independent families with five new biallelic loss-of-function and one previously reported recurrent EMC10 variants.

evidence.reference_title: A recurrent, homozygous EMC10 frameshift variant is associated with a syndrome of developmental delay with variable seizures and dysmorphic features.
evidence.snippet: The single-nucleotide deletion occurs in a homopolymeric repeat sequence (CGGGGC) that predisposes to DNA replication errors and represents a potential hotspot for genetic variation.

nodes.description: Homozygous Emc10 knockout mice phenotyped by the International Mouse Phenotyping Consortium show changes in vocalization, gait, activity and open-field behaviour. A separate Mirta22/Emc10 loss-of-function line showed no change in prepulse inhibition, working memory or social memory, and reducing Emc10 rescued those deficits in a 22q11.2 deletion model, where Emc10 is upregulated. Neither line has been assessed for the cognitive and seizure phenotypes of the human disorder.

evidence.reference_title: A recurrent, homozygous EMC10 frameshift variant is associated with a syndrome of developmental delay with variable seizures and dysmorphic features.
evidence.snippet: Differences include abnormal vocalization, gait, activity, and behavior during open field testing, which measures motor activity and anxiety-related behaviors in rodents

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutation in Mirta22/Emc10 rescues specific schizophrenia-related phenotypes in a mouse model of the 22q11.2 deletion.
evidence.snippet: Additional analysis of homozygous Mirta22 knockout mice, in which no alteration is observed in the above-mentioned SCZ-related phenotypes, highlights the deleterious effects of Mirta22 up-regulation.

nodes.description: Delay across social, motor, language and cognitive domains, mild to severe, with infantile onset in most individuals. Counts in both cohorts pool developmental delay with intellectual disability (11/12 and 10/10), so no frequency is assigned to this narrower term.

evidence.snippet: EMC10-related neurodevelopmental disorder (EMC10-NDD) is characterized by moderate-to-severe developmental delay and mild-to-severe intellectual disability.

nodes.description: Intellectual disability ranging from mild to severe. All five children of one extended family met diagnostic criteria for intellectual disability on formal testing, with verbal abilities below visuospatial abilities.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic loss of EMC10 leads to mild to severe intellectual disability.

nodes.description: Seizures in 6/13 individuals of the discovery cohort, usually in the neonatal period or childhood, including multifocal and generalized tonic-clonic seizures. In the follow-up cohort, complex partial seizures and subclinical tonic seizures were reported in two families.

evidence.reference_title: EMC10-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder.
